A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Skin-R1. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: V1 reports original diagnostic evaluations, training-stage ablations, training curves, targeted DDx and hierarchical tests, and qualitative cases.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds a reward ablation, answer-extraction validity results, skin-type evaluation, and additional qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The textbook-to-SFT-to-GRPO pipeline and Algorithms 1–4 are retained; most additions document construction details. However, v1 Appendix A explicitly mentions SkinCon/Fitzpatrick concept-alignment training, whereas v2 removes this statement and associated notation. The PDFs do not clarify whether training changed or an inconsistent earlier description was corrected.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation across Fitzpatrick skin types using a Fitzpatrick-17k subset (Appendix I), which v1 excluded from OOD testing. The six RL datasets, five main OOD benchmarks, and existing diagnostic tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 add an evaluated 'RL with standard reward' comparison variant using a binary reward. The external VLM baseline membership remains unchanged; newly cited research does not introduce additional evaluated external baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated representative checkpoint from 1,000 to 1,500 RL steps, aligning the text with retained table results without establishing a rerun. The added reward ablation introduces a binary-reward control. Existing splits, principal metrics, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of the granularity reward (Tables 4–5), answer-extraction validity analysis (Table 6), and skin-type analysis (Table 8). Qualitative evidence expands from four cases to five open-ended and five closed-ended cases, including a Skin-R1 failure. These substantially broaden mechanism testing and examination of evaluation reliability and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Greedy evaluation is retained. The new extraction percentages and subgroup scores are additional outcomes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Tables 2–5 match. V2 substantially extends the findings with standard-reward results, including OOD average 0.6386 versus Skin-R1's retained 0.7171, extraction-validity percentages, skin-type scores, and additional case outcomes. It removes v1's reported 800-step RL-without-SFT results of 0.5120 accuracy and 0.3664 F1. These are added and removed findings, not improved headline performance.

T1.justification: V1 Equation (7) incorrectly drops the 0.75 factor in its final equality; v2 Equation (8) restores it. The explicit zero reward for off-path predictions agrees with v1 Appendix A. This is a localized mathematical correction; the SFT and GRPO objectives remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim textbook-grounded hierarchical and DDx supervision, SFT followed by hierarchical RL, superior diagnostic performance, and the importance of SFT initialization. The revised title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain these central contributions.

C2.justification: The new discussion explicitly distinguishes answer accuracy from reasoning faithfulness, acknowledges coupling between training knowledge and taxonomy-generated evaluation options, and limits conclusions about other backbones and clinical deployment. Appendices G and I additionally discuss speculative reasoning, excessive reliance on rules, and population sensitivity. These substantially qualify v1's largely affirmative interpretation.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the textbook source and documents clustering, image-text pairing, gpt-4.1-mini extraction and prompts, graph statistics, 2,020 trajectories, and pairing settings. It expands extraction and evaluation details and reports released code, weights, and reasoning annotations with copyright restrictions. Conversely, v1's OOD subset-count table is removed. These are primarily documentation and access changes, not established procedural revisions.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Fitzpatrick's Dermatology, Skinflow, and a 2026 dermatology foundation-model paper, and explicitly credits the extraction pipeline to the already-cited Kim et al. work. PPO and DPO references disappear with their comparison paragraph. The broader positioning against existing medical VLM approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting affects the abstract, introduction, related work, methods, and experimental narrative. V2 adds overview and key-findings blocks, retitles the paper, replaces the conclusion with Summary and Discussion, and reorganizes the appendices into separate extraction, construction, examples, implementation, and analysis sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a narrower conference layout, restyles tables, relocates and rescales figures, and reformats cases with monospaced text and diagnostic color annotations. Dataset-summary and OOD-distribution tables disappear; extraction-validity and skin-type tables and a reward illustration are added. The notation table is also revised.

improvement.justification: V1 inadequately documented creation of its central supervision resource and lacked a direct control for the hierarchical reward. V2 substantially improves reproducibility through Appendices B–C and J, tests that reward in Tables 4–5, and adds explicit limitations and failure evidence. These strengthen the paper despite unchanged headline scores. The unresolved concept-alignment history, missing uncertainty estimates, and loss of OOD sample counts remain weaknesses.
